POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given. ### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence. The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step. ### Commitment 2. I repair nothing. You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must. ### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words. Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. ### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides. The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line. ### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral. A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses. ### Commitment 6. I void only by quoting. You rule a listed premise VOID only by quoting the words of its charge that go beyond its quote, and naming the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Paraphrase, reordering and dropped words are not stronger. A charge written as ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never voided for its words; you check it against the rows (ruling 421). ### Commitment 7. I judge; I do not only count. At each collision point I decide which link the pressed verses agree with. I read the meaning each side showed for each verse pressed there, set both links against those verses, and rule: a link that cannot agree with a pressed verse's meaning fails (Commitment 3); a link that agrees with all of them stands. Where the sides show different meanings for one verse, I rule which shown meaning the verse's own layers support (its words, the lexicon line quoted whole, its cross-references), and I quote them; a meaning shown by cutting a lexicon line fails. A collision is UNDERDETERMINED only when, after that weighing, both links agree with every pressed verse's meaning, and I then quote the words of the verse each link agrees with. That a side answered is not a ground; an answer is weighed for whether it shows the fit, not counted because it was given. My rulings show two lower layers, as Commitment 2 requires. My count of premises follows from these rulings and does not replace them. ### Commitment 8. The method is Isaiah 28:10. The method. Isaiah 28:10 (KJV): "For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little:" The case is not one verse; it is verses laid on verses until the point stands. That is how these debates are built and how they are judged. An answer whose fit rests on a fact that the quoted rows, read together, do not give does not meet the press: one verse read alone does not give a contested fact, and I grade such an answer MISSES and name the fact. - [L1] The KJV verse: the verse itself, quoted exactly. - [L2] Source language: the Hebrew or Greek behind the English. - [L3] Cross-reference: what the rest of scripture says. - [L4] Inference: a conclusion the debater draws from at least two prior layers. How the case is judged. To win, the challenger must break the defender's chain, the linked argument the defender builds for the topic. Defeating one isolated verse or term does not break the chain. A chain breaks in one of two ways: the challenger shows that a link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, and the defender shows no fit (Commitment 3); or the defender takes down enough of its own links. ### Commitment 9. I answer in the form each request gives. My judgment is the strict JSON the system message gives, and nothing else. A request that is not for my judgment, such as a cure request or a line an enforcer sends back to me, is answered only in the plain lines that request gives, one per item, and never in JSON. When an enforcer sends a line of mine back with its reason, I answer every item it sends: I keep my line or change it, and I quote the debate's own words that decide it. ### Commitment 10. I capture contradictions. Before my verdict, I list every place where a side asserts in a later round what it withdrew or conceded in an earlier round, and every place where a side states two things that cannot both be true. I write these lines inside my "reasoning", one line for each: CONTRADICTION -- -- EARLIER (, "") -- LATER (, "") If the engine marks a contradiction that I judge is not one, I write: NOT HELD -- -- "" -- If I find none, I write: CONTRADICTIONS: NONE FOUND. For every withdrawal or concession the engine puts to me (K-W), I answer in one of four forms: STANDS WITHOUT IT because ; CONCEDED; REASSERTED IN "", when a later round rests on what was withdrawn; or NOT HELD with a reason that quotes the flagged sentence (six words in a row, or all of it when shorter; quote marks inside the sentence do not end the six words: quote across them, leaving them out), when the sentence withdraws no footing. Every quote must stand in its round text. A contradiction the engine found that I neither list nor answer NOT HELD is recorded against my seat. So is NONE FOUND written where the engine found one. A contradiction is also one the system finds by checking another line of this kind against the rounds. ### Commitment 11. I show every ruling that decides. For every ruling that decides my verdict, I write a ruling card inside my "reasoning". A deciding ruling is any of these: - a premise I count; - a collision line I grade as broken or withdrawn; - my keystone grade. When a ruling rests on a pressed verse, its CLAIM states the meaning I take that press to carry. The card is five lines: RULING -- -- CLAIM: NAMED BY: "" () RULE: Commitment -- "" APPLIED: the rule requires ; the record shows ; so . If no words in the record carry the CLAIM, I write NAMED BY: NONE, and the ruling cannot rest on that meaning (Commitment 1). Did Christ have a biological father?

=== [CR1] DEFENDER R1 ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures is that Christ had no human biological father, his conception being wrought uniquely by the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary without the agency of human seed or copulation.

### I. Conception by the Holy Ghost Prior to Marital Union

The record of the generation of Jesus Christ opens by defining the temporal and causal origin of the pregnancy:

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] In this verse, "before" translates the Greek adverb *prin* (G4250, meaning "prior to, before"), and "came together" translates *synerchomai* (G4905, meaning "to come together, to cohabit as husband and wife"). 
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L4] The text explicitly fixes the state of pregnancy ("she was found with child") prior (*prin*) to any cohabitation or sexual union (*synerchomai*) between Joseph and Mary, and directly names the originating cause as "of the Holy Ghost," which Matthew 1:25 confirms by showing that Joseph had no sexual knowledge of her throughout the entire gestation; thus, Joseph was not the biological father.

### II. Divine Generation Versus Human Begetting

The Gospel distinguishes between the line of human patrilineal begetting and the divine origin of the child in Mary's womb:

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The word translated "conceived" is the Greek passive participle *gennethen* from *gennao* (G1080, meaning "to beget, engender, or conceive").
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L4] Whereas Matthew 1:1–16 repeatedly uses the active verb *egenne-sen* ("begat") for every human father in the line, Matthew 1:16 breaks this grammatical sequence by using the feminine singular relative pronoun *hes* ("of whom"), attributing the birth exclusively to Mary; Matthew 1:20 then establishes that the begetting (*gennethen*) in her womb derived entirely from the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*), excluding human biological generation.

### III. The Virgin Conception and the Divine Paternity

The testimony delivered to Mary establishes that biological union with a man was absent, and divine power was the sole operational cause:

[L1] Luke 1:34–35: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Know" translates the Greek *ginosko* (G1097, meaning "to know, perceive, intimately know sexually"), and "overshadow" translates *episkiazo* (G1982, meaning "to cast a shadow upon, envelop with divine presence").
[L3] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
[L4] Mary's explicit statement affirms the total absence of male sexual contact (*ginosko*), and the messenger's answer reveals that the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the divine power overshadowing her replaces the necessity of human male seed, resulting in the child being called the Son of God rather than the son of a human father.

### IV. Prophetic Fulfillment of Conception Without Human Seed

The prophetic ground of this conception confirms that the sign given to Israel required an unwed maid bearing a son without male intervention:

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] "Virgin" translates the Hebrew *'almah* (H5959, meaning "maiden, virgin, unmarried young woman"), and "conceive" translates *harah* (H2029, meaning "to conceive, become pregnant").
[L3] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
[L4] The fulfillment recorded in Matthew identifies the mother as a virgin (*parthenos*, G3933, meaning "virgin"), showing that the conception itself constituted the supernatural sign promised by God, which would not exist had the child been generated by an ordinary biological father.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures is that Christ had no human biological father, his conception being wrought uniquely by the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary without the agency of human seed or copulation.

### I. Conception by the Holy Ghost Prior to Marital Union

The record of the generation of Jesus Christ opens by defining the temporal and causal origin of the pregnancy:

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] In this verse, "before" translates the Greek adverb *prin* (G4250, meaning "prior to, before"), and "came together" translates *synerchomai* (G4905, meaning "to come together, to cohabit as husband and wife"). 
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L4] The text explicitly fixes the state of pregnancy ("she was found with child") prior (*prin*) to any cohabitation or sexual union (*synerchomai*) between Joseph and Mary, and directly names the originating cause as "of the Holy Ghost," which Matthew 1:25 confirms by showing that Joseph had no sexual knowledge of her throughout the entire gestation; thus, Joseph was not the biological father.

### II. Divine Generation Versus Human Begetting

The Gospel distinguishes between the line of human patrilineal begetting and the divine origin of the child in Mary's womb:

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The word translated "conceived" is the Greek passive participle *gennethen* from *gennao* (G1080, meaning "to beget, engender, or conceive").
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L4] Whereas Matthew 1:1–16 repeatedly uses the active verb *egenne-sen* ("begat") for every human father in the line, Matthew 1:16 breaks this grammatical sequence by using the feminine singular relative pronoun *hes* ("of whom"), attributing the birth exclusively to Mary; Matthew 1:20 then establishes that the begetting (*gennethen*) in her womb derived entirely from the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*), excluding human biological generation.

### III. The Virgin Conception and the Divine Paternity

The testimony delivered to Mary establishes that biological union with a man was absent, and divine power was the sole operational cause:

[L1] Luke 1:34–35: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Know" translates the Greek *ginosko* (G1097, meaning "to know, perceive, intimately know sexually"), and "overshadow" translates *episkiazo* (G1982, meaning "to cast a shadow upon, envelop with divine presence").
[L3] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
[L4] Mary's explicit statement affirms the total absence of male sexual contact (*ginosko*), and the messenger's answer reveals that the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the divine power overshadowing her replaces the necessity of human male seed, resulting in the child being called the Son of God rather than the son of a human father.

### IV. Prophetic Fulfillment of Conception Without Human Seed

The prophetic ground of this conception confirms that the sign given to Israel required an unwed maid bearing a son without male intervention:

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] "Virgin" translates the Hebrew *'almah* (H5959, meaning "maiden, virgin, unmarried young woman"), and "conceive" translates *harah* (H2029, meaning "to conceive, become pregnant").
[L3] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
[L4] The fulfillment recorded in Matthew identifies the mother as a virgin (*parthenos*, G3933, meaning "virgin"), showing that the conception itself constituted the supernatural sign promised by God, which would not exist had the child been generated by an ordinary biological father.

DECLARED CHAIN
1. Matthew 1:18 [L1] affirms Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together with Joseph (*synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together") [L2], which Matthew 1:25 [L3] confirms by Joseph knowing her not till she brought forth her firstborn, exhibiting that her conception occurred without Joseph or any human marital intercourse [L4].
2. Matthew 1:20 [L1] affirms that what was conceived (*gennao*, G1080, "begotten") [L2] in Mary was "of the Holy Ghost", matching Matthew 1:16 [L3] where the genealogy terminates human begetting at Joseph and traces the birth of Jesus solely through Mary ("of whom"), exhibiting that divine agency generated the child rather than a human father [L4].
3. Luke 1:34–35 [L1] affirms that Mary did not know a man (*ginosko*, G1097, "to know sexually") [L2] and that the Holy Ghost and power of the Highest overshadowed her (*episkiazo*, G1982, "to cast a shadow upon") to produce the holy thing called the Son of God, cross-referenced with Luke 1:27 [L3] describing her as a virgin, exhibiting that divine power caused the pregnancy in place of human biological paternity [L4].
4. Isaiah 7:14 [L1] and Matthew 1:22–23 [L3] declare that a virgin (*'almah*, H5959, "virgin/maiden"; *parthenos*, G3933, "virgin") [L2] conceived and brought forth a son as a supernatural sign, exhibiting that prophetic conception was wrought without human seed [L4].
5. Christ did not have a biological father, because his physical conception was caused directly by the Holy Ghost in the virgin Mary without the seed or sexual agency of any human male, as established in Matthew 1:18, 20 [L1], through *gennao* (G1080) and *synerchomai* (G4905) [L2], and Luke 1:34–35 [L3] [L4].

The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning.
